result.title: Conformally Calibrated Adaptive Computation in Neural Operators
result.summary: Selecting less computation in a neural operator need not reduce inference time. We study this gap using conformal calibration to choose Fourier modes or channel width per input subject to a fixed error budget. A triangle-inequality envelope bounds all candidates simultaneously; a direct-score rule handles non-monotone candidate errors and, with an input-independent score, calibrates a static baseline under the same marginal guarantee. Under frozen-model and exchangeability assumptions, both rules bound the probability of issuing a prediction outside the budget and abstain when calibration is infeasible. On Burgers and Darcy flow across three training seeds, mode selection reduces active spectral support without a measurable latency reduction, because full-grid transforms and channel mixing dominate the cost. Narrowing channels does reduce Darcy forward cost, but reference-based selection must first compute the dense prediction. An input-only binary width selector avoids that pass and runs at 0.52-0.95 times dense latency; yet static widths calibrated under the same rule are often as fast or faster, and on a separately generated 1,000-example test set they generally achieve higher coverage, while the selector falls below its 90% target in more than half of the settings. Adaptive computation in neural operators should therefore be judged by achieved coverage and complete runtime against a matched static comparator.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在神经算子中用 conformal calibration 按输入选择 Fourier 模态数或通道宽度，在固定误差预算下给出候选选择的统一误差包络与弃答规则，并在 Burgers、Darcy 上报告模态选择并未带来可测的延迟下降、静态宽度常与自适应选择一样快或更快。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按输入分配计算＋误差预算约束下的弃答/停止」表述与按覆盖率、完整运行时间对照匹配静态基线来检验自适应收益的做法，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的成本核算与停止决策评价提供可核查的框架线索，但领域为 PDE 算子推理，需核查迁移性。
